newsitem.title: INDIA: India's RBI issues revised commercial paper norms.
newsitem.headline: India's RBI issues revised commercial paper norms.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) issued revised norms for issue of commercial papers on Tuesday.
The Non-Banking Companies (acceptance of deposits through commercial papers) Directions 1989 circular has been amended for the purpose, the RBI said in a letter to banks on Tuesday.

It was desirable to allow highly rated corporate borrowers to diversify their sources of short-term borrowings by issue of commercial paper and also provide an additional financial instrument to investors, RBI said.
The following are some of the highlights of the letter.
+ Working capital limit of the company (issuing commercial papers) should not be less than 40 million rupees.
+ Aggregate amount to be raised by issue of commercial paper shall not exceed the working capital limit sanctioned by banks to the issuing company.
+ Working capital limit would include purchase/discount of bills sanctioned by one or more banking companies for meeting working capital requirements.
+ Working capital will not include facilities such as letters of credit, guarantees where there is no actual outlay of funds as well as credit limits sanctioned for acquisition of fixed assets.
+ The total amount of commercial paper proposed to be issued shall be raised within a period of two weeks from the date on which the proposal is taken on record by the financing bank.
+ It may be issued on a single date or in parts on different dates provided that in each case the commercial paper will have the same maturity date.
+ No company shall have the issue of commercial paper underwritten or co-accepted in any manner.
